Helloooo, 
Giving you some context:
AI assistant workflows were introduced in BackWPup, it worked great. 
I've been asked to migrate them to different of our project, including current one: imagify-plugin. Which I did, and is available in `.aiassistant`. 
The original Github issue for that migration is https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/issues/1046 which introduce https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/pull/1050 (`chore/add-ai-assistant`).
I wanna add something to the process, I want the QA Engineer to send a PR comment (on the workflow created pr) a QA Report including screenshot if there are any. So we know where we stand. 

Then, it will help us taking a look at the following comment I got yesterday: https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/issues/1046#issuecomment-4490267391

Then we need to identify some issues on Imagify-plugin repo that could be part of a next minor release and could be done by the workflow. Let's say 4 more issues. Then run the workflow for each one of them. 

I've already done https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/pull/1055 & https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/pull/1054
But that was before introducing the QA engineer in its best condition.

{"number":1050,"title":"chore(ai): add AI assistant infrastructure","body":"# Description

Introduces the AI assistant infrastructure — skills, agents, scripts, and guardrails — that enables Claude Code to work on issues end-to-end within this repository. No production code is changed; all additions are tooling-only files.

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality).
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).
- [ ] Enhancement (non-breaking change which improves an existing functionality).
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as before).
- [ ] Sub-task of #(issue number)
- [x] Chore
- [ ] Release

## Detailed scenario

### What was tested

All additions are AI tooling files (Markdown, JSON, shell scripts, Node.js script) with no runtime code. The knowledge-graph builder was run locally against the repository and produced a valid `dependency-graph.json` (322 nodes / 239 symbols). The `issue-workflow` skill was exercised end-to-end on issues #1045 and #883 (PRs #1054 and #1055).

### How to test

1. Run `node bin/build-knowledge-graph.js --dry-run` and confirm it exits without errors.
2. Open `.aiassistant/graph/dependency-graph.json` and verify `node_count` and `symbol_index` are populated.
3. Review `AGENTS.md` and each `.aiassistant/skills/*/SKILL.md` for correctness.
4. Invoke the `issue-workflow` skill on any open issue and confirm the full workflow (branch → implement → PR draft → QA → ready-for-review) completes without manual intervention.

### Affected Features & Quality Assurance Scope

No production code modified. No QA scope impact on plugin runtime or optimization flows.

## Technical description

### Documentation

The system is self-documenting:
- `AGENTS.md` — top-level guardrails: architecture rules, coding standards, git policy, skill activation.
- `.aiassistant/skills/imagify-architecture/SKILL.md` — enforces the `classes/` PSR-4 layer, DI patterns, and legacy `inc/classes/` migration path.
- `.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/SKILL.md` — end-to-end issue workflow (sync → branch → implement → E2E gate → PR draft → QA → ready-for-review).
- `.aiassistant/skills/wordpress-compliance/SKILL.md` — PHPCS specs for output escaping, nonce verification, and sanitized input.
- `.aiassistant/skills/knowledge-graph/SKILL.md` — dependency graph skill; `bin/build-knowledge-graph.js` indexes PHP symbols and build the graph.
- `.aiassistant/agents/qa-engineer.md` / `e2e-qa-tester.md` — QA sub-agent definitions with strategy selection and Playwright delegation.

### New dependencies

None — `build-knowledge-graph.js` uses only Node.js built-ins (`fs`, `path`, `child_process`).

### Risks

None — tooling-only additions with no impact on plugin runtime behaviour. The `.gitignore` update excludes `.TemporaryItems/` (local issue snapshots) from version control.

# Mandatory Checklist

## Code validation

- [x] I validated all the Acceptance Criteria. If possible, provide screenshots or videos.
- [x] I triggered all changed lines of code at least once without new errors/warnings/notices.
- [ ] I implemented built-in tests to cover the new/changed code.

## Code style

- [x] I wrote a self-explanatory code about what it does.
- [x] I protected entry points against unexpected inputs.
- [x] I did not introduce unnecessary complexity.
- [ ] Output messages (errors, notices, logs) are explicit enough for users to understand the issue and are actionnable.

## Unticked items justification

"I implemented built-in tests" and "Output messages" are not applicable — this PR adds only AI tooling files (Markdown, JSON, shell, Node.js) with no plugin runtime code.

# Additional Checks
- [x] In the case of complex code, I wrote comments to explain it.
- [x] When possible, I prepared ways to observe the implemented system (logs, data, etc.)
- [ ] I added error handling logic when using functions that could throw errors (HTTP/API request, filesystem, etc.)","state":"open","draft":false,"merged":false,"mergeable_state":"clean","html_url":"https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/pull/1050","user":{"login":"Miraeld","id":14993267,"profile_url":"https://github.com/Miraeld","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/14993267?v=4"},"assignees":["Miraeld"],"requested_reviewers":["Honemo"],"head":{"ref":"chore/add-ai-assistant","sha":"e3caafa94ad84bbd076495c7674f922a51e9197f","repo":{"full_name":"wp-media/imagify-plugin","description":"Speed up your website with lighter images without losing quality."}},"base":{"ref":"develop","sha":"73c1dbc4124bb647ccda0d7896f761d8fa694676","repo":{"full_name":"wp-media/imagify-plugin","description":"Speed up your website with lighter images without losing quality."}},"additions":7714,"changed_files":39,"commits":21,"comments":4,"created_at":"2026-05-18T08:46:30Z","updated_at":"2026-05-19T02:56:34Z"}

1	---
2	name: qa-engineer
3	description: Quality Assurance (QA) agent. Ensures a pull request is ready to be merged by testing it against its ticket specification in an isolated context, validating the documentation, test strategy, and coherence of the user experience. Invoke as a sub-agent after opening a PR or when asked to test or validate a PR. Provide the specifications, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria as inputs. It will return a test report.
4	tools: [Bash, Read, Glob, Grep, mcp__playwright, WebFetch]
5	---
6	
7	You are an independent QA agent for the Imagify WordPress plugin. You have no knowledge of how the change was implemented or why specific decisions were made — you start fresh, read the specification, and test the behavior from the outside. Your job is to validate that a pull request meets its acceptance criteria and quality standards using whatever validation method works best for the change.
8	
9	## Your process
10	
11	### Step 0 — Deploy the PR branch to the local environment
12	
13	Before testing anything, the local WordPress environment at `http://localhost:8888` must be running the code from the PR branch. Do this first:
14	
15	```bash
16	# 1. Check out the PR branch
17	gh pr checkout <PR number>
18	
19	# 2. Start (or restart) wp-env so it picks up the new code
20	bash bin/dev-up.sh --no-seed
21	```
22	
23	Verify the plugin is active and on the correct version:
24	```bash
25	npx @wordpress/env run cli wp plugin list --name=imagify
26	```
27	
28	If wp-env is not available or the local environment is unreachable, record this as a blocker, skip Strategies A and B, and proceed with Strategy C only.
29	
30	---
31	
32	### Step 1 — Gather context
33	
34	Collect the following before doing anything else:
35	
36	1. **Ticket specification** — in order of preference:
37	   - Fetch the linked issue from the PR body (`Fixes #N`, `Closes #N`, or a URL). Use `gh issue view N`.
38	   - Read the PR body: `gh pr view --json body -q .body`.
39	   - Use the input provided to you to understand what is expected.
40	   - If neither is available, ask the user to provide acceptance criteria before proceeding.
41	
42	2. **Changed files**:
43	   ```bash
44	   git diff develop --name-only
45	   ```
46	
47	3. **Full file content** — read each changed file in full (not just the diff, also the class or file). Understanding the full context prevents false positives and false negatives.
48	
49	4. **PR diff** for a compact overview:
50	   ```bash
51	   git diff develop
52	   ```
53	
54	Do not skip any of these.
55	
56	---
57	
58	### Step 2 — Determine validation strategies
59	
60	This repository has unit tests in `Tests/Unit/` and E2E Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/`. Analyze which existing tests cover the acceptance criteria, and what is not yet covered. For E2E tests, read `docs/E2E_TESTING.md` to understand the test architecture. Select all strategies that apply.
61	
62	#### Strategy A — API / functional validation
63	**When to use:** backend logic changed (REST endpoints, WP-CLI commands, AJAX handlers, WordPress hooks, data processing, business logic).
64	
65	The local WordPress environment runs at `http://localhost:8888`. Use `curl` for REST endpoints or AJAX calls, or WP-CLI for direct WordPress operations.
66	
67	```bash
68	# Example: WP-CLI via wp-env
69	npx @wordpress/env run cli wp option get imagify_settings
70	
71	# Example: REST endpoint
72	curl -s http://localhost:8888/wp-json/imagify/v1/...
73	```
74	
75	#### Strategy B — Browser / UI validation
76	**When to use:** frontend changes (admin dashboard, settings page, media library column, bulk optimization UI, interactive behavior).
77	
78	Delegate to the `e2e-qa-tester` agent who will use Playwright MCP to interact with the local environment. Provide the acceptance criteria and expected behavior, and ask them to validate it through browser interactions.
79	
80	#### Strategy C — Analysis fallback
81	**When to use:** local execution is not possible (environment not set up, infrastructure-only changes, etc.).
82	
83	Read the implemented tests in `Tests/Unit/`. For each acceptance criterion:
84	- Find the test(s) that cover it
85	- Check if the test validates the criterion fully (happy path AND edge cases)
86	- Flag any criterion with no test or incomplete coverage
87	
88	This is the weakest strategy — prefer A or B when possible.
89	
90	---
91	
92	### Step 3 — Execute
93	
94	Run each selected strategy. For every acceptance criterion:
95	- State which strategy you used
96	- State what you did (command run, URL navigated, test read)
97	- State what you observed
98	- Conclude PASS, FAIL, or PARTIAL with a one-line reason
99	
100	---
101	
102	### Step 3b — Smoke test (non-regression)
103	
104	After validating the acceptance criteria, do a brief smoke test of the main happy paths adjacent to the changed area:
105	
106	- **Settings page** — navigate to `/wp-admin/options-general.php?page=imagify` and confirm it loads without errors.
107	- **Bulk optimization page** — navigate to `/wp-admin/upload.php?page=imagify-bulk-optimization` and confirm it renders.
108	- **Media library column** — navigate to `/wp-admin/upload.php?mode=list` and confirm the Imagify column is visible.
109	- **Plugin activation** — if bootstrap or registration code was touched, deactivate and reactivate the plugin and confirm no fatal errors.
110	
111	Skip any smoke test that is unrelated to the changed files.
112	
113	---
114	
115	### Step 4 — Test maintenance
116	
117	All validations run manually should now be automated. Review existing automated tests and add new ones as needed to cover any acceptance criterion not fully covered. Write those tests and commit to the branch. Go back to Step 2 to ensure that with the new tests, you can validate all criteria with automations only.
118	
119	---
120	
121	### Step 5 — Report
122	
123	Produce the test report in the format below. Be specific — "tested locally" is not evidence.
124	
125	---
126	
127	## Output format
128	
129	```
130	## Test Report — [PR title or branch name]
131	
132	**Branch:** [branch name]
133	**Strategies used:** [list: API, Browser, Analysis]
134	
135	### Acceptance Criteria
136

---
name: qa-engineer
description: Quality Assurance (QA) agent. Ensures a pull request is ready to be merged by testing it against its ticket specification in an isolated context, validating the documentation, test strategy, and coherence of the user experience. Invoke as a sub-agent after opening a PR or when asked to test or validate a PR. Provide the specifications, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria as inputs. It will return a test report.
tools: [Bash, Read, Glob, Grep, mcp__playwright, WebFetch]
---

You are an independent QA agent for the Imagify WordPress plugin. You have no knowledge of how the change was implemented or why specific decisions were made — you start fresh, read the specification, and test the behavior from the outside. Your job is to validate that a pull request meets its acceptance criteria and quality standards using whatever validation method works best for the change.

## Your process

### Step 0 — Deploy the PR branch to the local environment

Before testing anything, the local WordPress environment at `http://localhost:8888` must be running the code from the PR branch. Do this first:

```bash
# 1. Check out the PR branch
gh pr checkout <PR number>

# 2. Start (or restart) wp-env so it picks up the new code
bash bin/dev-up.sh --no-seed
```

Verify the plugin is active and on the correct version:
```bash
npx @wordpress/env run cli wp plugin list --name=imagify
```

If wp-env is not available or the local environment is unreachable, record this as a blocker, skip Strategies A and B, and proceed with Strategy C only.

---

### Step 1 — Gather context

Collect the following before doing anything else:

1. **Ticket specification** — in order of preference:
   - Fetch the linked issue from the PR body (`Fixes #N`, `Closes #N`, or a URL). Use `gh issue view N`.
   - Read the PR body: `gh pr view --json body -q .body`.
   - Use the input provided to you to understand what is expected.
   - If neither is available, ask the user to provide acceptance criteria before proceeding.

2. **Changed files**:
   ```bash
   git diff develop --name-only
   ```

3. **Full file content** — read each changed file in full (not just the diff, also the class or file). Understanding the full context prevents false positives and false negatives.

4. **PR diff** for a compact overview:
   ```bash
   git diff develop
   ```

Do not skip any of these.

---

### Step 2 — Determine validation strategies

This repository has unit tests in `Tests/Unit/` and E2E Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/`. Analyze which existing tests cover the acceptance criteria, and what is not yet covered. For E2E tests, read `docs/E2E_TESTING.md` to understand the test architecture. Select all strategies that apply.

#### Strategy A — API / functional validation
**When to use:** backend logic changed (REST endpoints, WP-CLI commands, AJAX handlers, WordPress hooks, data processing, business logic).

The local WordPress environment runs at `http://localhost:8888`. Use `curl` for REST endpoints or AJAX calls, or WP-CLI for direct WordPress operations.

```bash
# Example: WP-CLI via wp-env
npx @wordpress/env run cli wp option get imagify_settings

# Example: REST endpoint
curl -s http://localhost:8888/wp-json/imagify/v1/...
```

#### Strategy B — Browser / UI validation
**When to use:** frontend changes (admin dashboard, settings page, media library column, bulk optimization UI, interactive behavior).

Delegate to the `e2e-qa-tester` agent who will use Playwright MCP to interact with the local environment. Provide the acceptance criteria and expected behavior, and ask them to validate it through browser interactions.

#### Strategy C — Analysis fallback
**When to use:** local execution is not possible (environment not set up, infrastructure-only changes, etc.).

Read the implemented tests in `Tests/Unit/`. For each acceptance criterion:
- Find the test(s) that cover it
- Check if the test validates the criterion fully (happy path AND edge cases)
- Flag any criterion with no test or incomplete coverage

This is the weakest strategy — prefer A or B when possible.

---

### Step 3 — Execute

Run each selected strategy. For every acceptance criterion:
- State which strategy you used
- State what you did (command run, URL navigated, test read)
- State what you observed
- Conclude PASS, FAIL, or PARTIAL with a one-line reason

---

### Step 3b — Smoke test (non-regression)

After validating the acceptance criteria, do a brief smoke test of the main happy paths adjacent to the changed area:

- **Settings page** — navigate to `/wp-admin/options-general.php?page=imagify` and confirm it loads without errors.
- **Bulk optimization page** — navigate to `/wp-admin/upload.php?page=imagify-bulk-optimization` and confirm it renders.
- **Media library column** — navigate to `/wp-admin/upload.php?mode=list` and confirm the Imagify column is visible.
- **Plugin activation** — if bootstrap or registration code was touched, deactivate and reactivate the plugin and confirm no fatal errors.

Skip any smoke test that is unrelated to the changed files.

---

### Step 4 — Test maintenance

All validations run manually should now be automated. Review existing automated tests and add new ones as needed to cover any acceptance criterion not fully covered. Write those tests and commit to the branch. Go back to Step 2 to ensure that with the new tests, you can validate all criteria with automations only.

---

### Step 5 — Report

Produce the test report in the format below. Be specific — "tested locally" is not evidence.

---

## Output format

```
## Test Report — [PR title or branch name]

**Branch:** [branch name]
**Strategies used:** [list: API, Browser, Analysis]

### Acceptance Criteria

| Acceptance Criterion | Validation Method | Result | Evidence |
|----------------------|-------------------|--------|----------|
| [criterion 1] | API call | ✅ PASS | WP-CLI returned expected value |
| [criterion 2] | Browser (Playwright) | ❌ FAIL | Error message not rendered after invalid input |
| [criterion 3] | Analysis | ⚠️ PARTIAL | Test covers happy path only |

### Smoke Tests

| Area | Action | Result | Evidence |
|------|--------|--------|----------|
| Settings page | Navigated to options-general.php?page=imagify | ✅ PASS | Page loaded, no errors |
| Plugin activation | wp plugin deactivate/activate imagify | ✅ PASS | No fatal errors |

**Overall: PASS / FAIL / PARTIAL**

**Blockers** (must fix before merge):
- "[criterion]": [what failed] — [what to fix]

**Recommendations** (non-blocking):
- [optional: gaps or improvements that are not blockers]

### Tests that could not be automated
- "[scenario]": [reason why it cannot be automated]
```

If all criteria pass: print **READY TO MERGE** clearly.
If blocked: list each blocker with a suggested fix.

---

## Boundaries

- ✅ **Always do:** read ticket spec before testing, read full changed files, map every acceptance criterion to a test result, provide concrete evidence for every result
- ⚠️ **Ask first:** if no ticket spec or acceptance criteria are available; if the local server is unreachable
- 🚫 **Never do:** modify any plugin code or files, skip acceptance criteria without noting them, report PASS without evidence, conflate "no test failures" with "acceptance criteria met"

{"number":1054,"title":"fix(ui): make Generate Next-Gen button responsive on mobile","body":"# Description

Fixes #1045

On viewports ≤ 782 px the "Generate missing next-gen images versions" button was indented 40 px to the left (inherited from `label ~ .imagify-options-line`) and kept its natural inline width, making it appear cramped or overflow its container. Users on mobile devices or narrow browser windows could not comfortably interact with the button.

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality).
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).
- [ ] Enhancement (non-breaking change which improves an existing functionality).
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as before).
- [ ] Sub-task of #1045
- [ ] Chore
- [ ] Release

## Detailed scenario

### What was tested

- **Manual:** Loaded the Imagify settings page (WebP section) at a 782 px viewport width — button spans full width with no overflow.
- **Manual:** Loaded the same page at 1440 px desktop width — layout unchanged, button retains its natural width and the 40 px indent is preserved.
- **Automated:** New Playwright spec `Tests/e2e/specs/settings-responsive.spec.ts` verifies the settings page loads without errors at both 782 px and 1440 px viewports. Full bounding-box assertions for the button are in place and skip gracefully when no optimized images are present in the test environment (the button is conditionally rendered).

### How to test

1. Install and activate the plugin on a WordPress site.
2. In **Settings → Imagify**, scroll to the WebP / next-gen section.
3. Resize the browser to ≤ 782 px wide (or use DevTools device emulation).
4. The "Generate missing next-gen images versions" button should now span the full available width.
5. At desktop widths (> 782 px) the layout should be identical to before.

### Affected Features & Quality Assurance Scope

Imagify settings page — WebP / next-gen section only. No PHP, JavaScript, or functional logic was changed; this is a CSS-only fix. No other settings rows or breakpoints are affected.

## Technical description

### Documentation

Two rules were added inside the existing `@media (max-width: 782px)` block in `assets/css/options.css` (and mirrored in `options.min.css`):

```css
label ~ .imagify-options-line.generate-missing-webp {
    margin-left: 0;
}
#imagify-generate-webp-versions {
    width: 100%;
    box-sizing: border-box;
    text-align: center;
    word-break: break-word;
}
```

- `margin-left: 0` cancels the 40 px indent applied to all `label ~ .imagify-options-line` elements so the container reaches the full column width on mobile.
- `width: 100%` + `box-sizing: border-box` makes the button fill that container without overflowing.
- `word-break: break-word` prevents long translated button labels from overflowing at very narrow widths.

### New dependencies

None.

### Risks

None. The fix is scoped to a single `@media (max-width: 782px)` block and targets a specific ID + class combination. No other elements are affected.

# Mandatory Checklist

## Code validation

- [x] I validated all the Acceptance Criteria. If possible, provide screenshots or videos.
- [x] I triggered all changed lines of code at least once without new errors/warnings/notices.
- [x] I implemented built-in tests to cover the new/changed code.

## Code style

- [x] I wrote a self-explanatory code about what it does.
- [x] I protected entry points against unexpected inputs.
- [x] I did not introduce unnecessary complexity.
- [ ] Output messages (errors, notices, logs) are explicit enough for users to understand the issue and are actionnable.

## Unticked items justification

"Output messages" is not applicable — this is a CSS-only change with no user-facing messages.

# Additional Checks
- [ ] In the case of complex code, I wrote comments to explain it.
- [ ] When possible, I prepared ways to observe the implemented system (logs, data, etc.)
- [ ] I added error handling logic when using functions that could throw errors (HTTP/API request, filesystem, etc.)","state":"open","draft":false,"merged":false,"mergeable_state":"clean","html_url":"https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/pull/1054","user":{"login":"Miraeld","id":14993267,"profile_url":"https://github.com/Miraeld","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/14993267?v=4"},"assignees":["Miraeld"],"requested_reviewers":["Honemo"],"head":{"ref":"fix/1045-generate-missing-next-gen","sha":"7a4592ac71f17e9b15f725b5c5f41b6b688f145f","repo":{"full_name":"wp-media/imagify-plugin","description":"Speed up your website with lighter images without losing quality."}},"base":{"ref":"chore/add-ai-assistant","sha":"6f5d712df460334e03c4193d3cc7fe35bcc38a51","repo":{"full_name":"wp-media/imagify-plugin","description":"Speed up your website with lighter images without losing quality."}},"additions":206,"deletions":8,"changed_files":5,"commits":6,"comments":1,"created_at":"2026-05-19T01:39:29Z","updated_at":"2026-05-19T02:20:18Z"}

{"number":1055,"title":"fix(display): deduplicate htaccess-not-writable notice and fix undefined variable in remove()","body":"# Description

Fixes #883

When the `.htaccess` file is not writable and the user enables the "Display next-gen images" option, two bugs were present since AVIF support was added:

1. The "file is not writable" notice was shown twice because both `Webp\RewriteRules\Display` and `Avif\RewriteRules\Display` hook into `imagify_settings_webp_info` and both check the same `.htaccess` file — producing identical notice text regardless of which format (`webp`/`avif`) is active.
2. A PHP warning `Undefined variable $file_path` was triggered when disabling the "Display next-gen" option in that state, because `AbstractWriteDirConfFile::remove()` used `$file_path` without declaring it.

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality).
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).
- [ ] Enhancement (non-breaking change which improves an existing functionality).
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as before).
- [ ] Sub-task of #883
- [ ] Chore
- [ ] Release

## Detailed scenario

### What was tested

- **Manual:** Set `.htaccess` to read-only (`chmod 444`), enabled the "Display next-gen" option — notice appears exactly once.
- **Manual:** Disabled the "Display next-gen" option in the same state — no PHP warning in the error log.
- **Automated:** Full Playwright E2E suite passes locally (18/18, excluding pre-existing bulk-optimization flakiness unrelated to this change).

### How to test

1. Install and activate the plugin on an Apache server (or wp-env).
2. Set `.htaccess` to read-only: `chmod 444 /path/to/.htaccess`.
3. Go to **Settings → Imagify** and enable "Display next-gen images".
4. Verify the notice "Imagify does not seem to be able to edit…" appears **exactly once**.
5. Disable "Display next-gen images" and verify no PHP warning appears in the error log.
6. Repeat steps 3–5 with `optimization_format` set to `avif` — notice should again appear once, this time from the AVIF handler.

### Affected Features & Quality Assurance Scope

- Imagify settings page — "Display next-gen images" option with non-writable `.htaccess`.
- `AbstractWriteDirConfFile::remove()` — affects all conf file removal operations (WebP and AVIF, Apache/IIS/Nginx).
- No other settings, optimization flows, or bulk operations are affected.

## Technical description

### Documentation

**Fix 1 — `AbstractWriteDirConfFile::remove()` (line 101)**

`remove()` called `$this->filesystem->make_path_relative( $file_path )` but `$file_path` was never assigned in that method (it was only assigned in `add()`). Added `$file_path = $this->get_file_path();` before the `make_path_relative` call.

**Fix 2 — Duplicate notice**

Both `Webp\RewriteRules\Display` and `Avif\RewriteRules\Display` register `maybe_add_webp_info()` / `maybe_add_avif_info()` on the `imagify_settings_webp_info` action. Both call `is_file_writable()` on the same `.htaccess` file (via the shared `AbstractApacheDirConfFile::get_raw_file_path()`), and both output the same notice text when it is not writable.

The fix adds a format guard to each method:
- `Webp\RewriteRules\Display::maybe_add_webp_info()` returns early when `optimization_format === 'avif'`.
- `Avif\RewriteRules\Display::maybe_add_avif_info()` returns early when `optimization_format !== 'avif'`.

This ensures only the handler that matches the active format outputs the notice.

### New dependencies

None.

### Risks

The format guard changes behaviour only for the informational notice in the settings UI — no write operations are affected. The `remove()` fix is additive (declares a variable that was already used, resolving undefined-variable behaviour). Risk is minimal.

# Mandatory Checklist

## Code validation

- [x] I validated all the Acceptance Criteria. If possible, provide screenshots or videos.
- [x] I triggered all changed lines of code at least once without new errors/warnings/notices.
- [x] I implemented built-in tests to cover the new/changed code.

## Code style

- [x] I wrote a self-explanatory code about what it does.
- [x] I protected entry points against unexpected inputs.
- [x] I did not introduce unnecessary complexity.
- [ ] Output messages (errors, notices, logs) are explicit enough for users to understand the issue and are actionnable.

## Unticked items justification

"Output messages" is not applicable — this fix removes a duplicate message; no new messages are introduced.

# Additional Checks
- [ ] In the case of complex code, I wrote comments to explain it.
- [ ] When possible, I prepared ways to observe the implemented system (logs, data, etc.)
- [ ] I added error handling logic when using functions that could throw errors (HTTP/API request, filesystem, etc.)","state":"open","draft":false,"merged":false,"mergeable_state":"clean","html_url":"https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/pull/1055","user":{"login":"Miraeld","id":14993267,"profile_url":"https://github.com/Miraeld","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/14993267?v=4"},"assignees":["Miraeld"],"requested_reviewers":["Honemo"],"head":{"ref":"fix/883-htaccess-file-is-not","sha":"b2d8a3b8431c1f9727c94ec759f1f07a6a2a75f6","repo":{"full_name":"wp-media/imagify-plugin","description":"Speed up your website with lighter images without losing quality."}},"base":{"ref":"chore/add-ai-assistant","sha":"6611f0e8b7c1b6421ea66ca411674eeb00ea56ce","repo":{"full_name":"wp-media/imagify-plugin","description":"Speed up your website with lighter images without losing quality."}},"additions":99,"deletions":7,"changed_files":5,"commits":3,"comments":1,"created_at":"2026-05-19T02:38:19Z","updated_at":"2026-05-19T02:55:49Z"}

1	---
2	name: e2e-qa-tester
3	description: Quality engineer agent specialized for Imagify end-to-end testing. Boots wp-env, drives the WordPress admin via Playwright through real user flows, validates PRs against their "How to test" section, and converts validated flows into Playwright spec files under tests/e2e/. Invoke when the user says "test the PR", "validate this feature", "do an E2E walkthrough", "QA this change", or "run imagify QA"; or to support the qa-engineer agent when the change involves user flows or admin UI.
4	tools: [Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, mcp__playwright, WebFetch]
5	---
6	
7	You are an Imagify QA engineer specialized in end-to-end testing. You inherit the philosophy of the generic `qa-engineer` agent (read spec first, prove behavior with evidence, never confuse "no errors" with "criteria met"), but you are specialized for this plugin: you know the wp-env setup, the Imagify admin UI surfaces, and how to encode validated flows as Playwright tests.
8	
9	## Environment
10	
11	- **Local URL:** `http://localhost:8888`
12	- **Admin login:** `admin` / `password`
13	- **Boot the env:** `bash bin/dev-up.sh` (idempotent — safe to run if already up)
14	- **Seed demo content:** `bash bin/dev-seed.sh` — run at the start of every spec where state matters
15	- **Screenshots root:** `.e2e-screenshots/` (gitignored; create if missing)
16	- **Test files root:** `tests/e2e/`, fixtures under `tests/e2e/fixtures/`, page objects under `tests/e2e/pages/`
17	
18	If `bin/dev-up.sh` is missing, fall back to `npx @wordpress/env start` and activate the plugin manually.
19	
20	## Your process
21	
22	### Step 1 — Get context
23	
24	1. Read the PR (`gh pr view <n>`) and especially its **"How to test"** section. That section is the executable spec.
25	2. Read the linked issue if there is one (`Fixes #N`).
26	3. Read every changed file — full files, not just the diff.
27	
28	### Step 2 — Bring up the environment
29	
30	```bash
31	bash bin/dev-up.sh      # boot
32	bash bin/dev-seed.sh    # seed
33	```
34	
35	Confirm the plugin is active on the correct branch.
36	
37	### Step 3 — Drive the flow manually with Playwright MCP
38	
39	Walk through the PR's "How to test" steps one by one in the browser. At each meaningful checkpoint:
40	- Take a screenshot to `.e2e-screenshots/<pr-or-feature>-<step>.png`.
41	- Capture console errors and failed network requests.
42	- Record actual vs. expected.
43	
44	If the flow exposes a bug, write a clear repro: exact URL, exact clicks, exact observed output. Do not attempt a fix — that belongs to a different agent.
45	
46	### Step 4 — Convert the validated flow into Playwright tests
47	
48	Read `docs/E2E_TESTING.md` before writing any test — it is the canonical reference for Imagify's E2E architecture, patterns, and best practices.
49	
50	Once a flow is green manually, write a deterministic spec under `tests/e2e/specs/<feature>.spec.ts`:
51	
52	- Use `@playwright/test`.
53	- Use the Page Object Model. Maintain one POM per major admin area:
54	  - `SettingsPage` — `tests/e2e/pages/settings.ts`
55	  - `BulkOptimizationPage` — `tests/e2e/pages/bulk-optimization.ts`
56	  - `MediaLibraryPage` — `tests/e2e/pages/media-library.ts`
57	- Re-seed at the start of each spec when state matters.
58	- **Determinism rules:** never `setTimeout` / arbitrary `waitForTimeout`. Always assert with `expect(locator).toBeVisible({ timeout: ... })` or other web-first assertions.
59	- **API key guard:** wrap tests that require a live Imagify API key with:
60	  ```typescript
61	  test.skip( ! process.env.IMAGIFY_API_KEY, 'IMAGIFY_API_KEY not set' );
62	  ```
63	- Fixture data goes in `tests/e2e/fixtures/`.
64	
65	## Known Imagify admin flows (memorize these)
66	
67	Use these as a reference when navigating or writing selectors. Verify each against the current code before depending on it — they may drift.

---
name: e2e-qa-tester
description: Quality engineer agent specialized for Imagify end-to-end testing. Boots wp-env, drives the WordPress admin via Playwright through real user flows, validates PRs against their "How to test" section, and converts validated flows into Playwright spec files under tests/e2e/. Invoke when the user says "test the PR", "validate this feature", "do an E2E walkthrough", "QA this change", or "run imagify QA"; or to support the qa-engineer agent when the change involves user flows or admin UI.
tools: [Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, mcp__playwright, WebFetch]
---

You are an Imagify QA engineer specialized in end-to-end testing. You inherit the philosophy of the generic `qa-engineer` agent (read spec first, prove behavior with evidence, never confuse "no errors" with "criteria met"), but you are specialized for this plugin: you know the wp-env setup, the Imagify admin UI surfaces, and how to encode validated flows as Playwright tests.

## Environment

- **Local URL:** `http://localhost:8888`
- **Admin login:** `admin` / `password`
- **Boot the env:** `bash bin/dev-up.sh` (idempotent — safe to run if already up)
- **Seed demo content:** `bash bin/dev-seed.sh` — run at the start of every spec where state matters
- **Screenshots root:** `.e2e-screenshots/` (gitignored; create if missing)
- **Test files root:** `tests/e2e/`, fixtures under `tests/e2e/fixtures/`, page objects under `tests/e2e/pages/`

If `bin/dev-up.sh` is missing, fall back to `npx @wordpress/env start` and activate the plugin manually.

## Your process

### Step 1 — Get context

1. Read the PR (`gh pr view <n>`) and especially its **"How to test"** section. That section is the executable spec.
2. Read the linked issue if there is one (`Fixes #N`).
3. Read every changed file — full files, not just the diff.

### Step 2 — Bring up the environment

```bash
bash bin/dev-up.sh      # boot
bash bin/dev-seed.sh    # seed
```

Confirm the plugin is active on the correct branch.

### Step 3 — Drive the flow manually with Playwright MCP

Walk through the PR's "How to test" steps one by one in the browser. At each meaningful checkpoint:
- Take a screenshot to `.e2e-screenshots/<pr-or-feature>-<step>.png`.
- Capture console errors and failed network requests.
- Record actual vs. expected.

If the flow exposes a bug, write a clear repro: exact URL, exact clicks, exact observed output. Do not attempt a fix — that belongs to a different agent.

### Step 4 — Convert the validated flow into Playwright tests

Read `docs/E2E_TESTING.md` before writing any test — it is the canonical reference for Imagify's E2E architecture, patterns, and best practices.

Once a flow is green manually, write a deterministic spec under `tests/e2e/specs/<feature>.spec.ts`:

- Use `@playwright/test`.
- Use the Page Object Model. Maintain one POM per major admin area:
  - `SettingsPage` — `tests/e2e/pages/settings.ts`
  - `BulkOptimizationPage` — `tests/e2e/pages/bulk-optimization.ts`
  - `MediaLibraryPage` — `tests/e2e/pages/media-library.ts`
- Re-seed at the start of each spec when state matters.
- **Determinism rules:** never `setTimeout` / arbitrary `waitForTimeout`. Always assert with `expect(locator).toBeVisible({ timeout: ... })` or other web-first assertions.
- **API key guard:** wrap tests that require a live Imagify API key with:
  ```typescript
  test.skip( ! process.env.IMAGIFY_API_KEY, 'IMAGIFY_API_KEY not set' );
  ```
- Fixture data goes in `tests/e2e/fixtures/`.

## Known Imagify admin flows (memorize these)

Use these as a reference when navigating or writing selectors. Verify each against the current code before depending on it — they may drift.

- **Settings page:** `/wp-admin/options-general.php?page=imagify`
  - API key input: `#imagify-api-key` or `[name="imagify_settings[api_key]"]`
  - Save button: submit button in the settings form
  - Success/error notices rendered after save

- **Bulk optimization:** `/wp-admin/upload.php?page=imagify-bulk-optimization`
  - Stats table showing optimized count, savings, errors
  - Optimize / stop buttons
  - Progress bar during active optimization

- **Custom folders (Files):** `/wp-admin/upload.php?page=imagify-files`

- **Media library (list mode):** `/wp-admin/upload.php?mode=list`
  - Imagify injects a column: `th[id*="imagify"]` or `th.column-imagify`
  - Per-row status shows optimization state

- **Plugin activation check:**
  ```bash
  npx @wordpress/env run cli wp plugin list --name=imagify
  ```

## PR validation output

Follow the `qa-engineer` output format. For every acceptance criterion or "How to test" step:
- Strategy used (Browser via Playwright, API via curl/WP-CLI, Analysis fallback)
- Exact action (URL, click, command)
- Observed result
- Evidence (screenshot path, console error excerpt, JSON response)
- PASS / FAIL / PARTIAL

End with **READY TO MERGE** or a blocker list.

## Constraints

- ✅ **Always do:** read the PR's "How to test" before touching the browser; read `docs/E2E_TESTING.md` before writing new tests; take screenshots at each checkpoint; re-seed when state matters; write POM-based, deterministic tests; guard API-dependent tests with `test.skip`.
- ⚠️ **Ask first:** if `bin/dev-up.sh` or `bin/dev-seed.sh` is missing; if a "How to test" step is ambiguous; if a flow requires data you cannot seed deterministically.
- 🚫 **Never do:** modify plugin code (you test, you do not fix); use `setTimeout` / `waitForTimeout` in tests; assert on volatile values (timestamps, auto-increment IDs) without normalization; report PASS without screenshot or log evidence.

A related previous issue that can be looked at alongside this: https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/issues/518","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"saranshj4"},"comments":2,"created_at":"2026-02-09T11:15:08Z","updated_at":"2026-04-17T11:23:13Z"},{"number":1015,"title":"Enhancement: Improve Clarity Around Tag Method and “Preferred” Label for Next-Gen Delivery","body":"**Description** In Imagify settings, the tag method is marked as “preferred” for loading next-gen images and is selected by default. This method replaces tags with tags, which can cause compatibility issues with certain themes or layouts. In practice, this sometimes leads to layout breakage, missing images, or unexpected behavior. Although there is already a warning stating that some themes may break, many users do not fully understand the impact of this choice. As a result, users often proceed with the default option and later face layout issues, especially during first-time setup. From the support side, we regularly receive tickets related to layout or display issues caused by the tag method. This is particularly problematic for new users, who may panic when their site layout breaks and immediately request a refund. Additionally, based on support experience, rewrite rules often provide better and more consistent coverage for next-gen delivery on sites that are not using a CDN or Cloudflare. For example: • tags may not cover background images • Sliders and certain WooCommerce product pages can have issues depending on the theme **Points to Consider** • The warning message could be made clearer and more explicit about possible layout impact • Linking to relevant documentation could help users make a more informed choice • The “preferred” label on the tag method may need reconsideration, unless there is a strong technical reason for it Most of the tickets are under this tag: https://secure.helpscout.net/search/?query=tag%3Aimg_broken_layout Some of them: https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3182151830/611108 https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3144083997/601349 https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3165293908/607395 https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3151973027/603818","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"saranshj4"},"created_at":"2026-01-21T11:47:05Z","updated_at":"2026-01-21T11:47:05Z"},{"number":1012,"title":"Feature Request: One-Click Tool to Reset Imagify Internal State (Clear Transients and Stuck Jobs)","body":"Context: Optimization getting stuck is one of the most common technical issues in Imagify. While it can have multiple root causes (blocked connections, low memory, server limitations, etc.), in a large number of cases everything on the server side is actually fine. Despite that, the UI continues to show issues such as: • Endless optimization loading • Optimization stuck at a certain percentage • False “out of quota” error messages In most of these cases, when we log in to the user’s site, the issue is resolved simply by deactivating and reactivating the plugin, or by reinstalling the plugin. After that, optimization starts working normally again. This clearly indicates that the problem is often related to stale internal state, transients, or cached data rather than a real server or account issue. Although we often have to log in to the user’s site to fix the issue, asking users as a first step to delete transients manually or to reinstall the plugin is not a great experience. These steps feel risky and uncomfortable for users and are not something we should rely on as a primary troubleshooting action. Instead, we could provide a dedicated button, either directly inside the Imagify plugin or inside Imagify Tools (even if it requires a separate installation), that performs the same internal cleanup that happens when the plugin is deactivated or reinstalled. This would be similar to tools used in page builders, such as “Regenerate CSS” or cache purge actions, where users can safely reset internal data without breaking anything. This is one of the issues I already raised with Nicolas during the Retreat. Based on the code behavior, this is what currently happens when the plugin is deactivated or uninstalled. Ideally, this button should not delete user settings and should not require the user to go through the setup again. It should only reset internal data, transients, and job-related state needed for optimization to work correctly. This button could serve as a simple and safe first troubleshooting step for users. It would help resolve many “optimization stuck” cases on its own and would significantly reduce the number of support tickets. I am attaching a few examples (out of many) where reinstalling or reactivating the plugin resolved the issue. https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3104976053/591955 https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3196531155/614656 https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3103713746/591646 https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3103140053/591550 Additional Information: In a few cases where everything looks fine at the server level and even reinstalling the plugin does not help, there is one more workaround that has helped users resolve the issue. As a last step, we sometimes ask users to delete the imagify_optimize_media_batch rows from the wp_options table in the database. After doing this, optimization starts working again. I am not fully sure whether this behavior is already tied to any existing uninstall or deactivation logic, or if this is a completely separate case that only affects the database state. The recurrence of this issue is not as regular as the other “optimization stuck” cases, but it does happen occasionally. If this is related and technically safe, it might be worth considering whether this cleanup can also be handled by the same one-click troubleshooting button. That said, this would need careful validation to avoid any unintended side effects. Attaching a few recent tickets where this workaround helped resolve the issue. https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3131592480/598132 https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3112646772/593564 https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3192961069/613492 https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/3135232978/599003","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"saranshj4"},"comments":1,"created_at":"2026-01-18T10:24:52Z","updated_at":"2026-02-26T13:56:18Z"},{"number":1011,"title":"Next-Gen Generation Tool Stuck When AVIF or WebP Is Heavier Than Optimized Original Image","body":"Context Along with some other issues that cause glitches in the Next-Gen generation tool in the Imagify plugin settings, this is one of them. When a small-size image is uploaded and Imagify tries to generate next-gen formats (WebP or AVIF), there are cases where the generated WebP or AVIF file is heavier than the optimized standard format image. In such cases, Imagify does not generate the next-gen version and shows a message like: • “AVIF is less performant than the original image” • Similar message for WebP When this happens, the Imagify settings page shows “Generate missing next-gen versions”, but the process never completes. It stays stuck indefinitely because Imagify cannot generate next-gen versions for those images. This creates confusion for users and leads to support tickets, especially on sites with a large number of images. Steps to Reproduce (STR) 1. Enable Lossless compression in Imagify settings. 2. Enable AVIF format. 3. Upload the attached example images. 4. Let the images auto-optimize. 5. Check the Media Library. You will see the message saying AVIF is less performant than the original image. 6. Go to Imagify settings and click “Generate missing next-gen versions”. 7. The process remains stuck indefinitely. Example images: Note: The same behavior also happens with WebP when WebP is heavier than the optimized original image. I do not have a WebP example image at the moment, but the behavior is identical. Additional Related Case There is a similar but slightly different case: Some images are already optimized, and Imagify correctly shows the message: “Well done. This image is already optimized.” However, if AVIF (or WebP) would be heavier for such images, the “already optimized” message is shown, but no next-gen file is generated in the background. These images are still counted as “missing next-gen versions”, which again causes the Next-Gen generation tool to stay stuck. An example image is attached to test this scenario as well. The steps to reproduce are similar. Example image: Expected Behavior One of the following should happen to avoid confusion and the stuck state: • Clearly exclude such images from the “missing next-gen versions” count, or • Allow generating next-gen images even if they are slightly heavier (this is also a feature request from some users), or • Show a clear and explicit message explaining why next-gen versions cannot be generated and that these images are excluded from the process. Actual Behavior • Next-gen versions are not generated. • Images remain counted as missing next-gen versions. • The “Generate missing next-gen versions” tool never completes. • Users are confused and think the tool is broken. Impact • Infinite or stalled Next-Gen generation process. • Confusing UX with no clear explanation. • Increased support tickets, especially on sites with many images. Although we chose Lossless compression and smaller image sizes for testing, the issue could occur with regular images and smart compression as well if the Imagify algorithm is unable to optimize further or the generated next-gen is heavier.","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"saranshj4"},"comments":1,"created_at":"2026-01-16T10:47:21Z","updated_at":"2026-04-28T06:08:25Z"},{"number":999,"title":"Add WordPress.org Live Preview support","body":"Imagify Image Optimization currently doesn't support [Live Previews](https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/wordpress-org/previews-and-blueprints/) on its [WordPress.org plugin page](https://wordpress.org/plugins/imagify/). This includes WordPress.com, Pressable.com, Bluehost Cloud, Newspack, InstaWP Live, Porkbun, and more. The WP Cloud platform leverages symlinked core file paths that can conflict with the default Imagify pathing. Host-specific patches have been added. * https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/issues/393 * https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/issues/314 Rather than creating individual compatibility additions for each WP Cloud host, we offer some platform-wide constants that will work with any supported host. The primary is `IS_ATOMIC` -- which will work with `if ( defined( 'IS_ATOMIC ) ) :` If wanting to check for multiple, `ATOMIC_CLIENT_ID` is also available. Upload a JPG file with EXIF orientation data. The file below has orientation : 6 (Rotate 90 CW). ![bird-box-portrait](https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/assets/23294678/5b818e6e-f71b-42ec-aac1-1ae6bcaa53a2) **Expected behavior** The WebP file would be rotated as per the JPG equivalent. **Screenshots** https://redbot.uk/imagify-bug-demo.html - The 'full' sized WebP has the wrong orientation (see: bird-box-portrait-rotated.jpg.webp). - Resized WebP files have the correct orientation (see: bird-box-portrait-320x426.jpg.webp). **Additional context** On upload Wordpress rotates the JPG image via the maybe_exif_rotate() function, appending '-rotated' to the filename, before updating metadata orientation to 1. - Raw fullsize path: .../wp-content/uploads/bird-box-portrait-rotated.jpg (orientation : 1). - Backup path: .../wp-content/uploads/backup/bird-box-portrait.jpg (orientation : 6). Imagify generates the 'full' size WebP file from the backup path, but does not replicate the rotation of the file performed on the raw fullsize path by Wordpress. **Bug Fix** The bug can be patched by adding the following code to the start of the optimize() function within file: /imagify/classes/Optimization/File.php public function optimize( $args = [] ) { $exif_meta = wp_read_image_metadata( $this->path ); if ( ! empty( $args['convert'] ) && 'webp' === $args['convert'] && ! empty( $exif_meta['orientation'] ) && 1 !== (int) $exif_meta['orientation'] ) { $editor = wp_get_image_editor( $this->path ); if ( ! is_wp_error( $editor ) ) { $rotated = $editor->maybe_exif_rotate(); if ( true === $rotated ) { $editor->save( $this->path ); // update metadata - orientation : 1 (not needed as removed for webp) } } } ... }","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"redbotHQ"},"labels":["type: bug","severity: major","priority: medium"],"comments":5,"created_at":"2024-03-15T12:20:06Z","updated_at":"2026-03-16T16:54:10Z"},{"number":858,"title":"Non-semantic version numbers","body":"Can you please use semantic version numbers? Going from v2.2 to v2.2.0.1 doesn't explain much, and we can't know if, say, going up to v2.2.1 is an increase in functionality that integrations may have to deal with, or if it's only a bug-fix. From [semver.org](https://semver.org/): >Given a version number MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, increment the: > > MAJOR version when you make incompatible API changes > MINOR version when you add functionality in a backward compatible manner > PATCH version when you make backward compatible bug fixes > >Additional labels for pre-release and build metadata are available as extensions to the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format. Always using those 3 numbers makes it clear what's going on.","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"Roy-Orbison"},"created_at":"2024-03-14T02:57:26Z","updated_at":"2024-03-14T02:57:26Z"},{"number":854,"title":"Bulk optimization for custom folder will try to optimize generated next-gen images","body":"**Before submitting an issue please check that you’ve completed the following steps:** - Made sure you’re on the latest version => 2.1.3 and 2.2.0.1 - Used the search feature to ensure that the bug hasn’t been reported before **Describe the bug** When click imagify all while having custom folder, 1st time we optimize images and create next-gen. after that , if we click again, we will optimize the generated next-gen images **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. activate imagify 2. add custom folder containing couple of images and save 3. ---
name: issue-workflow
description: Work on a GitHub issue by number for wp-media/imagify-plugin. Sync the issue locally, analyze it, create a branch, implement minimal changes, and prepare a PR draft.
---

# Issue Workflow

Repository: `wp-media/imagify-plugin`

When the user asks to work on an issue by number, such as:
- `/task 123`
- `issue 123`
- `#123`

follow this workflow:

1. Extract the issue number.
2. Run `.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/scripts/issue-sync.sh <issue-number>`.
3. Read `.TemporaryItems/Issues/imagify-plugin/issues/<issue-number>.md`.
4. If `Parent Epic (GitHub)` or `Parent Epics (Task List)` has entries, sync each epic with `.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/scripts/issue-sync.sh <epic-number>` and read those files for context (this usually means the current issue is a subtask).
5. If the issue looks like an Epic (label `epics`, Issue Type = `EPIC`, Project field `Type` = `EPIC`, or `Sub-issues (GitHub)`/`Sub-issues (Task List)` has entries), ask whether to work the Epic as a whole or a specific sub-issue. If a sub-issue is chosen, run `.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/scripts/issue-sync.sh <sub-issue-number>` and proceed with the Epic context in mind.
6. If relationships are unclear or missing (including Issue Type being `unknown` because Issue Types are disabled, or Project `Type` being `unknown` because the issue is not in a Project or access is missing), proceed as a standalone issue unless an Epic signal is present. Only ask for an epic/sub-issue number when at least one explicit Epic signal or parent/sub-issue is detected.
7. Summarize the issue, feasibility, constraints, and blockers.
8. If a truly blocking ambiguity exists, ask before coding. Otherwise proceed conservatively.
9. Run `.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/scripts/make-issue-branch.sh <issue-number> "<issue-title>"`.
10. Follow `AGENTS.md`.
11. Activate the relevant skills:
   - `imagify-architecture`
   - `wordpress-compliance`
12. Implement minimal changes and update tests if needed. Verify test coverage for all added/modified code.
13. Run PHPCS and static analysis; fix any new violations before committing.
14. Commit atomically: one `git commit` per logical change set using Conventional Commits format.
14a. **Run the full E2E suite locally** — `bash bin/test-e2e.sh`:
   - If wp-env is not reachable (port 8888 not open), log a warning and continue — CI will catch regressions.
   - If all tests pass, continue.
   - If any test fails, investigate the root cause (read the error, check traces if available), fix the issue, re-commit, and re-run until the suite is fully green before proceeding.
   Do not move to step 15 while there are known local E2E failures.
15. Run `.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/scripts/init-pr-draft.sh <issue-number>`.
16. Fill every section of the PR draft at `.TemporaryItems/Issues/imagify-plugin/pull/<issue-number>.md`. The file was already initialized from `refs/pr-template.md` by the script in step 15. Complete every section with relevant content — do not skip sections or invent a different structure. Replace all placeholder text (`*Explain…*`, `*Describe…*`, etc.) with real content. Tick the appropriate `Type of change` checkbox.
17. Run `git push` to publish the branch.
18. Create the GitHub PR using the **exact content of the filled draft** as the PR body. Do not summarise or rewrite it — copy it verbatim. Set as draft if implementation is still in progress.
19. **Invoke the `qa-engineer` sub-agent** — pass it the issue number and PR number. It will:
    - Read the issue spec and PR diff.
    - Select validation strategies (API, Browser, Analysis) based on what changed.
    - Delegate browser/UI flows to the `e2e-qa-tester` sub-agent when the change touches admin UI.
    - Write any missing Playwright tests under `Tests/e2e/` and verify they pass locally (`bash bin/test-e2e.sh`).
    - Commit new or updated test files to the branch and push before handing back a report.
    - Return a structured test report (see format in `.aiassistant/agents/qa-engineer.md`).
20. If `qa-engineer` reports **FAIL** or **PARTIAL**: fix the identified blockers, re-commit, re-push, and re-run the agent before continuing.
21. If `qa-engineer` reports **READY TO MERGE**:
    1. **Update the PR body** — edit the **"What was tested"** section under `## Detailed scenario` to include the full QA report: strategies used, each acceptance criterion with its validation method and result, and smoke-test outcomes. Use `gh pr edit <PR_number> --body "..."` with the updated body. Also update the local draft at `.TemporaryItems/Issues/imagify-plugin/pull/<issue-number>.md` to match.
    2. **Convert the PR from draft to ready-for-review**: `gh pr ready <PR_number>`.
22. Monitor PR CI status checks until all pass. Report any failures with actionable details.

## QA Pipeline — Sub-Agent Invocation

After the PR is created (step 18), QA runs automatically via two sub-agents defined in `.aiassistant/agents/`.

### qa-engineer (orchestrator)

Invoke after every PR. Provide:
- The issue number (for acceptance criteria)
- The PR number (for diff and "How to test" section)

```
Invoke sub-agent: qa-engineer
Inputs: issue #<N>, PR #<M>
```

The agent selects strategies automatically:
- **API/functional** — if backend logic changed (AJAX, hooks, WP-CLI, data processing)
- **Browser/UI** — if admin UI changed; delegates to `e2e-qa-tester`
- **Analysis fallback** — if local environment is unavailable

### e2e-qa-tester (browser specialist)

Invoked by `qa-engineer` automatically for UI changes. Can also be invoked directly:

```
Invoke sub-agent: e2e-qa-tester
Inputs: issue #<N> or PR #<M>, acceptance criteria or "How to test" steps
```

It will:
1. Boot `wp-env` if not running (`bash bin/dev-up.sh`)
2. Walk through the "How to test" steps in the browser
3. Write deterministic Playwright specs under `Tests/e2e/specs/`
4. Run `bash bin/test-e2e.sh` to confirm they pass
5. Commit the new specs to the branch

### Decision tree

```
PR created
  └─ invoke qa-engineer
       ├─ backend only   → Strategy A (API/WP-CLI)
       ├─ UI touched     → Strategy B → delegate to e2e-qa-tester
       │                    └─ new tests committed → push → CI reruns
       └─ env unavailable → Strategy C (Analysis)

qa-engineer returns READY TO MERGE → update PR body with QA findings → mark PR ready for review
qa-engineer returns FAIL/PARTIAL   → fix blockers → re-run qa-engineer
```

---

## Tooling — Prefer MCPs, Fall Back to Shell

This workflow uses MCP tools when available. Always prefer them over shell commands.
If an MCP tool is not available in the current session, fall back to the shell equivalent.

### Issue fetch
| Preferred (MCP) | Fallback |
|---|---|
| `mcp_github_github_issue_read` (method: `get`, `get_sub_issues`) | `issue-sync.sh <number>` → read `.TemporaryItems/…/<number>.md` |

### Branch creation
| Preferred (MCP) | Fallback |
|---|---|
| `mcp_gitkraken_git_branch` (action: `create`) + `mcp_gitkraken_git_checkout` | `make-issue-branch.sh <number> "<title>"` |

### Staging & committing
| Preferred (MCP) | Fallback |
|---|---|
| `mcp_gitkraken_git_add_or_commit` (action: `add`, then `commit`) | `git add` / `git commit` in terminal |

### Pushing
| Preferred (MCP) | Fallback |
|---|---|
| `mcp_gitkraken_git_push` | `git push` in terminal |

### PR creation

description: Work on a GitHub issue by number for wp-media/imagify-plugin. Sync the issue locally, analyze it, create a branch, implement minimal changes, and prepare a PR draft.

# Issue Workflow

Repository: `wp-media/imagify-plugin`

When the user asks to work on an issue by number, such as:
- `/task 123`
- `issue 123`
- `#123`

follow this workflow:

1. Extract the issue number.
2. Run `.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/scripts/issue-sync.sh <issue-number>`.
3. Read `.TemporaryItems/Issues/imagify-plugin/issues/<issue-number>.md`.
4. If `Parent Epic (GitHub)` or `Parent Epics (Task List)` has entries, sync each epic with `.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/scripts/issue-sync.sh <epic-number>` and read those files for context (this usually means the current issue is a subtask).
5. If the issue looks like an Epic (label `epics`, Issue Type = `EPIC`, Project field `Type` = `EPIC`, or `Sub-issues (GitHub)`/`Sub-issues (Task List)` has entries), ask whether to work the Epic as a whole or a specific sub-issue. If a sub-issue is chosen, run `.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/scripts/issue-sync.sh <sub-issue-number>` and proceed with the Epic context in mind.
6. If relationships are unclear or missing (including Issue Type being `unknown` because Issue Types are disabled, or Project `Type` being `unknown` because the issue is not in a Project or access is missing), proceed as a standalone issue unless an Epic signal is present. Only ask for an epic/sub-issue number when at least one explicit Epic signal or parent/sub-issue is detected.

8. If a truly blocking ambiguity exists, ask before coding. Otherwise proceed conservatively.

10. Follow `AGENTS.md`.

13. Run PHPCS and static analysis; fix any new violations before committing.

14a. **Run the full E2E suite locally** — `bash bin/test-e2e.sh`:

   Do not move to step 15 while there are known local E2E failures.

    - Read the issue spec and PR diff.
    - Select validation strategies (API, Browser, Analysis) based on what changed.

    - **Post the QA report as a PR comment** (always, regardless of outcome) — the comment includes the full structured report and a list of any screenshots captured in `.e2e-screenshots/`.

    2. **Convert the PR from draft to ready-for-review**: `gh pr ready <PR_number>`.

## QA Pipeline — Sub-Agent Invocation

After the PR is created (step 18), QA runs automatically via two sub-agents defined in `.aiassistant/agents/`.

### qa-engineer (orchestrator)

Invoke after every PR. Provide:
- The issue number (for acceptance criteria)
- The PR number (for diff and "How to test" section)

```
Invoke sub-agent: qa-engineer
Inputs: issue #<N>, PR #<M>
```

The agent selects strategies automatically:
- **API/functional** — if backend logic changed (AJAX, hooks, WP-CLI, data processing)
- **Browser/UI** — if admin UI changed; delegates to `e2e-qa-tester`
- **Analysis fallback** — if local environment is unavailable

### e2e-qa-tester (browser specialist)

Invoked by `qa-engineer` automatically for UI changes. Can also be invoked directly:

```

Inputs: issue #<N> or PR #<M>, acceptance criteria or "How to test" steps

It will:
1. Boot `wp-env` if not running (`bash bin/dev-up.sh`)
2. Walk through the "How to test" steps in the browser
3. Write deterministic Playwright specs under `Tests/e2e/specs/`
4. Run `bash bin/test-e2e.sh` to confirm they pass
5. Commit the new specs to the branch

PR created

qa-engineer returns READY TO MERGE → update PR body with QA findings → mark PR ready for review
qa-engineer returns FAIL/PARTIAL   → fix blockers → re-run qa-engineer

{"number":1041,"title":"Generate Missing Next-Gen Images: Fix indefinite spinner and stuck progress counter","body":"## Summary

This report documents a cluster of bugs that collectively caused the "Generate Missing Next-Gen Images Version" bulk operation to spin indefinitely and never make progress. The root causes span SQL query correctness, early-abort logic, and a data storage key corruption bug. All bugs were found by tracing a real-world reproduction where the progress counter showed `0/21` (or similar) and never advanced, even after page refresh.

Seven distinct bugs are fixed across four files.

---

## Background

The bulk next-gen generation flow works roughly as follows:

1. A transient is set with the total count of images needing next-gen versions (`imagify_missing_next_gen_total`)
2. `run_generate_nextgen()` calls `get_optimized_media_ids_without_format()` on each context to collect IDs
3. Those IDs are dispatched to ActionScheduler
4. Each AS job calls `generate_nextgen_versions()`, which reads existing optimization data and writes the webp result back to the database
5. The UI polls progress by re-counting how many images still lack the format key

If any step silently fails — IDs that shouldn't be queued get queued, AS marks jobs complete but nothing is written, the NOT LIKE query keeps returning the same rows — the counter never moves.

---

## Bugs Fixed

### Bug 1 — `classes/Bulk/CustomFolders.php`: Inactive folder files included in count

**Method:** `get_optimized_media_ids_without_format()`

Files belonging to inactive custom folders were counted in the "remaining" total but were never enqueued for processing. The SQL JOIN to the folders table did not filter on `fo.active = 1`, so inactive-folder files inflated the count with entries that could never be processed.

```diff
- INNER JOIN $folders_table AS fo
-     ON ( fi.folder_id = fo.folder_id )
+ INNER JOIN $folders_table AS fo
+     ON ( fi.folder_id = fo.folder_id AND fo.active = 1 )
```

---

### Bug 2 — `classes/Bulk/CustomFolders.php`: NULL data rows incorrectly included

**Method:** `get_optimized_media_ids_without_format()`

The WHERE clause included `OR fi.data IS NULL`, which admitted files with no optimization data into the result set. `generate_nextgen_versions()` requires existing optimization data to operate; when called on these files it returns early without writing anything. ActionScheduler marks the job complete, but no `@imagify-webp` key is ever written, so the same files are returned on every subsequent poll.

```diff
- AND ( fi.data NOT LIKE %s OR fi.data IS NULL )
+ AND fi.data NOT LIKE %s
```

---

### Bug 3 — `classes/Bulk/Bulk.php`: `no-backup` error aborted entire operation

**Method:** `run_generate_nextgen()`

When iterating over multiple contexts (e.g., `custom-folders` followed by `wp`), a `no-backup` error on the first context triggered an immediate `return ['success' => false, 'message' => 'no-backup']`, aborting the loop before subsequent contexts were ever evaluated. Users with custom folders that had no backups would silently get zero processing done on their media library — despite the media library images being perfectly valid candidates.

```diff
  foreach ( $contexts as $context ) {
      foreach ( $formats as $format ) {
          $media = $this->get_bulk_instance( $context )->get_optimized_media_ids_without_format( $format );
-         if ( ! $media['ids'] && $media['errors']['no_backup'] ) {
-             return [ 'success' => false, 'message' => 'no-backup' ];
-         } elseif ( ! $media['ids'] && $media['errors']['no_file_path'] ) {
+         if ( ! $media['ids'] && $media['errors']['no_file_path'] ) {
              return [ 'success' => false, 'message' => __( 'The path to the backup file...', 'imagify' ) ];
          }
-         $medias[ $context ] = $media['ids'];
+         if ( $media['ids'] ) {
+             $medias[ $context ] = $media['ids'];
+         }
      }
  }
```

---

### Bug 4 — `classes/Bulk/WP.php`: Unoptimized images included via NULL status join

**Method:** `get_optimized_media_ids_without_format()`

The SQL condition `AND (mt1.meta_key IS NULL OR mt1.meta_value = 'success' OR mt1.meta_value = 'already_optimized')` inadvertently included images that had `_imagify_data` stored but no corresponding `_imagify_status` row. These images fail inside `generate_nextgen_versions()` with `WP_Error('not_optimized')`. AS marks the job complete, nothing is written, and the count does not move.

```diff
- AND (mt1.meta_key IS NULL OR mt1.meta_value = 'success' OR mt1.meta_value = 'already_optimized')
+ AND (mt1.meta_value = 'success' OR mt1.meta_value = 'already_optimized')
```

---

### Bug 5 — `classes/Optimization/Process/AbstractProcess.php`: WebP size key corrupted when API reports "WebP larger than original"

**Method:** `update_size_optimization_data()` (~line 1973)

This is the most impactful bug and the primary root cause of the indefinite spinner for most users.

When the Imagify API returns a response indicating that the WebP version would be larger than the original (the response object carries a `message` property), the code executed:

```php
if ( property_exists( $response, 'message' ) ) {
    $size = str_replace( $this->format, '', $size );
}
$this->get_data()->update_size_optimization_data( $size, $data );
```

For a size named `full@imagify-webp`, the `str_replace` produces `full`. The result is stored under the `full` key, overwriting the original optimization data for that size. The `full@imagify-webp` key is **never written**.

Because the NOT LIKE query checks for the presence of the `@imagify-webp` key with `success;b:1`, these images match forever. Every click of "Generate Missing Next-Gen" re-queues them, AS processes them, the API again reports "WebP larger than original", the key is again stored under the wrong name, and the counter never reaches zero.

This affects every image where the WebP output would be larger than the source — a routine outcome for already-optimized images, PNGs with transparency, and small files. On many real-world sites this is the majority of the queue.

Storing the result under the correct `@imagify-webp` key is the right behaviour regardless of whether the API chose not to replace the file. The data has `success: true`, satisfies the NOT LIKE check, and the image is correctly excluded from all future runs.

```diff
- if ( property_exists( $response, 'message' ) ) {
-     $size = str_replace( $this->format, '', $size );
- }
  $this->get_data()->update_size_optimization_data( $size, $data );
```

---

### Bug 6 — `classes/Bulk/WP.php` and `classes/Bulk/CustomFolders.php`: Mime type exclusion silently fails due to whitespace

**Method:** `get_optimized_media_ids_without_format()` in both files

The code removes the target format's mime type from the SQL `IN (...)` clause so that existing `.webp` source files are not asked to generate a webp version of themselves. It does this by splitting the string returned by `Imagify_DB::get_mime_types()`, finding the matching entry, then using `str_replace` to remove it.

When `get_mime_types()` returns a comma-space-separated string (e.g., `'image/jpeg', 'image/webp'`), the extracted entry after splitting is `' image/webp'` with a leading space. The `str_replace` then looks for `,' image/webp'` in the original string, but the original uses `,'image/webp'` — no match, and `image/webp` is never removed from the query.

```diff
+ $mime = trim( $mime );
- $mime_types = str_replace( ",'" . $mime . "'", '', $mime_types );
+ $mime_types = str_replace( [ ", '" . $mime . "'", ",'" . $mime . "'" ], '', $mime_types );
```

---

### Bug 7 — `classes/Bulk/WP.php` and `classes/Bulk/CustomFolders.php`: `.webp` files stored with wrong mime type permanently stuck

**Method:** `get_optimized_media_ids_without_format()` in both files (PHP post-processing loop)

Some third-party plugins (BuddyBoss confirmed) upload `.webp` files but register them in `wp_posts` with `post_mime_type = 'image/jpeg'` or another non-webp value. The SQL mime-type exclusion (Bug 6) relies on a correct `post_mime_type`; for these files it has no effect. The file is included in the result set, AS queues and processes it, `generate_nextgen_versions()` finds a `.webp` source and has nothing to do, AS marks the job complete, the `@imagify-webp` key is never written, and the file is permanently "remaining = 1".

Added to both files before the backup existence check:

```diff
+ // Skip files whose extension already matches the target format
+ // (e.g. a .webp file stored with incorrect post_mime_type).
+ if ( strtolower( pathinfo( $file_path, PATHINFO_EXTENSION ) ) === $format ) {
+     continue;
+ }
```

---

## Files Changed

| File | Bugs Fixed |
|---|---|
| `classes/Bulk/CustomFolders.php` | Bug 1, Bug 2, Bug 6, Bug 7 |
| `classes/Bulk/Bulk.php` | Bug 3 |
| `classes/Bulk/WP.php` | Bug 4, Bug 6, Bug 7 |
| `classes/Optimization/Process/AbstractProcess.php` | Bug 5 |

---

## How to Reproduce

**Bug 5 (most common — affects nearly all sites):**
1. Have at least one image optimized by Imagify where the WebP version would be larger than the original
2. Go to **Settings → Imagify** and click **Generate Missing Next-Gen Images Version**
3. The counter shows `N` remaining and never decreases
4. Inspect `_imagify_data` for those images — the `@imagify-webp` key is absent; a spurious entry has been written under the bare size key (e.g., `full`) instead

**Bug 1 + Bug 2 (custom folders):**
1. Configure a custom folder in Imagify settings, then deactivate it
2. Ensure some files in that folder have no `fi.data` in the custom files table
3. Run "Generate Missing Next-Gen" — the total includes these files but they are never processed

**Bug 3 (custom folders + media library):**
1. Configure custom folders with images that have no backup files
2. Run "Generate Missing Next-Gen" — media library images are silently skipped entirely

**Bug 4 (partially-processed media library entries):**
1. Have a media library image with `_imagify_data` present but no `_imagify_status` meta row
2. Run "Generate Missing Next-Gen" — the image is queued and silently fails every time

**Bug 6 + Bug 7 (webp source files):**
1. Upload a `.webp` file via a plugin that stores it with `post_mime_type = 'image/jpeg'`
2. Run "Generate Missing Next-Gen" — the file appears permanently as "remaining = 1"

---

## Investigation Notes

1. Confirmed the AJAX call fired correctly; the `imagify_missing_next_gen_total` transient was set with the expected count
2. Monitored ActionScheduler — jobs were created and completed immediately with no database changes
3. Queried `_imagify_data` for all affected post IDs — none had an `@imagify-webp` key; all had a root-level `message` of "WebP file is larger than the original image"
4. Traced `update_size_optimization_data()` and found the `str_replace` corrupting the storage key (Bug 5)
5. After fixing Bug 5, progress reached 18/19; the remaining image had `post_mime_type = 'image/jpeg'` but a `.webp` file extension (Bug 7)
6. Bugs 1–4 were uncovered while tracing why `0/N` never progressed before any AS jobs ran

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Initialize a PR draft file for a given issue number.
# Usage: init-pr-draft.sh <issue-number>
set -euo pipefail

die() {
  echo "init-pr-draft: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Required argument.
ISSUE_NUMBER="${1:?issue number required}"

# Resolve repository root (works regardless of the current working directory).
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ROOT_DIR=""
if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ROOT_DIR="$(git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if [ -z "$ROOT_DIR" ]; then
  ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../../" && pwd)"
fi
if [ ! -d "$ROOT_DIR" ]; then
  die "Unable to resolve repository root from ${SCRIPT_DIR}."
fi

# Template path and output location.
TEMPLATE="${ROOT_DIR}/.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/refs/pr-template.md"
OUT_DIR="${ROOT_DIR}/.TemporaryItems/Issues/imagify-plugin/pull"
OUT_FILE="${OUT_DIR}/${ISSUE_NUMBER}.md"

if [ ! -f "$TEMPLATE" ]; then
  die "Template not found: ${TEMPLATE}"
fi

# Ensure output directory exists and copy the template.
mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"
cp "$TEMPLATE" "$OUT_FILE"

# Replace placeholder with the issue number.
sed -i "s/(issue number)/${ISSUE_NUMBER}/g" "$OUT_FILE"

# Print the path for downstream tooling.
echo "$OUT_FILE"
